title: An eval gate for the 90 day warranty · a sketch for Rather Labs by Juan Pablo García
desc: An eval gate on every AI change, so a fix for one answer cannot quietly break ten others during the warranty.
h1: An eval gate for AI features under a 90 day warranty
lede: You take AI MVPs to production and cover each launch with a 90 day warranty on bugs and incidents. With LLM features, a fix for one answer can quietly break ten others, and a normal test suite will not notice. This is the gate I would put on every AI change, so the warranty costs less and the client sees why.
stage: From real traffic to a release you can defend

flow.label: Diagram of an evaluation gate that scores every AI change against a golden set before it ships

nodes.s: case by case vs last release

steps.d: Logs from the MVP plus the cases the client is nervous about. For a product like TranscribeMe that means domain terms, crosstalk and accents.

steps.t: A golden set, not a demo
steps.d: A few hundred inputs with what good looks like. Some are checked exactly, some by a rubric the client signs off on.
A shorter prompt, a cheaper model, a new chunking rule or a library bump. All of them can move outputs.

steps.t: Score it on every pull request
steps.d: Accuracy, grounding in the source, latency and cost per call. It runs in CI on recorded responses, so repeating it is cheap and does not need API keys.
The gate compares each case with the last release. A better average that hides five broken cases does not pass.

steps.t: Ship with a diff, or stop
steps.d: What improved, what got worse and why, in a short report the client can read. Or a list of the exact cases that blocked it.
Every incident in the 90 days becomes a new case, so the same bug cannot come back in the next release.
